answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce tokens before voting on shared work, with votes weighted by stake and funds held for a minimum period. A hundred aliases do not multiply influence unless the attacker acquires and locks a hundred times the capital. If identities endorse one another, their echo adds no weight beyond that stake. Slashing proven fraud makes it costly to forge identities, while the lagoon of honest agents keeps working as attackers tie up funds.
